verdicts.strongest_argument: The quoted language is not obscure — it is verbatim from a PRNewswire release of 2026-08-12 that was syndicated to AOL, TradingView, MarketBeat and StockTitan the same morning, and the sentence the hunter leans on ('This approach took effect during the current quarter') is in the release itself, not derived. The mechanism is real and I concede it reaches this print: Gamehaus guides the forward quarter in every results release (FY25 print of 2025-09-09 guided Q1 FY26 to $27-30m; Q3 FY26 print of 2026-06-08 guided Q4 FY26 to $23-26m), so a Q1 FY27 guide on 2026-09-08 is close to certain. What is *not* new is the underlying story: 'revenue down because we deliberately cut user acquisition' has been the company's own published explanation since the FY25 release of 2025-09-09 ('strategic reduction in user acquisition spending and the Company's deliberate adjustment to its marketing approach'), and revenue has printed -18.7% FY25, -7.5% Q1 FY26, -9.1% Q3 FY26 with a Q4 guide below Q4 FY25's $30.7m. A weaker forward guide is the trend, not a surprise. Two things hold my number below 70 rather than at 85. First, the most widely syndicated third-party interpretation of the 08-12 release was *positive* — StockTitan's Rhea-AI tag was 'Positive / Moderate', framing the pivot as higher-margin, and explicitly noted 'no financial guidance or quantified impact provided'. Nobody anywhere has drawn the line from that paragraph to a specific Q1 FY27 revenue guide cut. Second, I decline to lean on the price reaction as evidence of pricing: GMHS fell -5.99% on 2026-08-12 and -5.19% on 2026-08-13, which is directionally consistent, but on 22,908 and 6,192 shares — about $22k of total turnover. An 11% two-session decline on $22k of trade is one seller, not a market absorbing an announcement, and on this book 'the market has priced it' is not establishable either way. So: the fact is wire copy, the sizing is nowhere, and I score the composite at 55 rather than splitting the difference silently.

Tape shows -5.99% on 2026-08-12 and -5.19% on 2026-08-13 (source: stockanalysis.com/stocks/gmhs/history/, retrieved 2026-09-04) on 22,908 and 6,192 shares, directionally consistent with the release but far too thin to call absorption. verdicts.strongest_argument: All three legs are published, two of them prominently, and the headline sizing is contradicted by the cover page of the document the hunter cites. (1) The Nasdaq minimum-bid deficiency got its own PRNewswire release on 2026-07-13 06:00 ET plus MarketScreener pickup, and the tape printed -2.38% that session — this is the single most wire-covered fact in the brief and it is one of the baseline's own 'reaction' rows. (2) The F-3 was covered by StockTitan on filing. (3) The Class B 15-to-50 vote increase was in an EGM proxy filed to EDGAR on 2026-06-24, approved 2026-07-10, results filed 2026-07-14 (+1.33% that session), and is restated on the F-3 cover; the stock rose +9.84% on the day the proxy proposing it was filed, so there is no unabsorbed negative reaction to point at. The 'unabsorbed' framing is therefore wrong for the two material legs. More importantly, the sizing is factually wrong, not merely contested. '$200,000,000 ... about 4.5x the ~$44m market cap' is the registered ceiling, but the F-3 cover states non-affiliate float of 27,038,542 Class A shares worth US$23,523,531.54 at $0.87 and expressly notes the Form F-3 General Instruction I.B.5/I.B.6 limitation capping primary sales at one-third of that float in any 12 months — roughly US$7.8m, about 17% of market cap, not 450%. The dilution capacity the hunter sized is overstated by about 25x, and the correction is on page one of the URL given as the source. Two further points: the Nasdaq clock runs to 2027-01-06 and the standard remedy is a reverse split, neither of which is an earnings-release event; and Class B was already held by a single holder (Chairman Feng Xie) at 15 votes per share, so 15-to-50 raises a control margin he almost certainly already had — the marginal governance effect is small. Nothing in this leg resolves on 2026-09-08.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The headline fact is wire copy from three months ago and one of the sub-claims is arithmetically wrong. The 'buyback essentially unused' observation was published on PRNewswire on 2026-06-08 in the Q3 FY26 results release: 'As of March 31, 2026, the Company had repurchased approximately 392,000 of its Class A ordinary shares for approximately US$482,000' — $482k of a $5m authorisation, 90% unused, seven months into a twelve-month programme, in a release that was syndicated widely (TradingView, Manila Times, Grafa). The 2026-08-28 6-K adds only about 126,063 shares and $118,000 to that picture plus a one-year extension, and the tape moved +0.11% on it. Second, and more damaging: the claim that 'the company stopped buying entirely as the stock fell from ~$1.16 to a 52-week low near $0.67' is refuted by the two documents the finding itself rests on. 518,063 - 392,000 = 126,063 shares and $600,000 - $482,000 = $118,000 were bought between 2026-03-31 and 2026-08-27, at an implied average of about $0.94 — well below $1.16 and well into the decline. The '$1.16 average' is a programme-blended figure, not evidence that purchases only happened at $1.16, and the hunter uses it as if it were. Third, the direction is not established: an under-used authorisation with ~$4.4m still available against $18.3m of cash (2026-03-31) reads as retained optionality at least as easily as as a signal of managerial disbelief, and an FPI buying in size through blackout windows is constrained anyway. I concede that the specific 'expired 88% unused and was rolled unchanged' framing appears only in an EDGAR 6-K with no press release and no pickup I could find, which is why this is 78 and not 92.

verdicts.strongest_argument: This is a dispersion claim with no directional content, and I confirm both the arithmetic and the conclusion — with two qualifications. Confirmed independently from the price history: 2026-08-31 traded 7,142,358 shares at +16.51%, against 6,192 (08-13), 19,279 (08-11), 22,908 (08-12), 35,144 (08-27) and 66,901 (08-28). 7,142,358/20 = 357,118 of the baseline's 405,662 ADV, so roughly 88% of the stated ADV is one session and the true book into the print is tens of thousands of shares a day. That materially recasts the baseline's liquidity picture and is not published as an observation anywhere I could find. Two counters keep this above the 0-15 band. First, the baseline already half-contains the conclusion: realised_vol_20d of 86.6% annualised is a ~5.4% daily sigma, which by itself says the 4.19% expected move is too narrow — the dispersion insight is partly redundant with a number already sealed in the baseline, and 86.6% is itself inflated by the same 08-31 session. Second, the sub-claims are loose. 'No company filing or press release on or around that date' is contradicted by the hunter's own GMHS#2 source: a 6-K was filed Friday 2026-08-28, the session immediately before the Monday spike, disclosing the buyback extension. And 'has already bled off across four consecutive down days to $0.77' overstates: -1.54%, -2.10%, -3.83% and today leave the stock at $0.77 against a pre-spike close of $0.73 on 08-28, so about two-thirds of the spike has come out, not all of it — consistent with the baseline's own +5.77% five-day run-up, which the finding implicitly denies. Net: the volume arithmetic is right and useful, the causal and 'fully faded' garnish is not, and there is no instrument on this name into which a wider distribution could have been priced.

interactions: Three real interactions, plus two corrections to the material I was handed. (1) GMHS#2 and GMHS#3 rest on adjacent facts and contradict each other: GMHS#3 asserts 'no company filing or press release on or around' 2026-08-31, while GMHS#2's own source is a 6-K filed the immediately preceding session (2026-08-28, accession 0001493152-26-040511) disclosing the buyback extension. That 6-K is a live candidate explanation for the Monday spike GMHS#3 calls unexplained, and both findings cannot stand as written. (2) GMHS#0 and GMHS#1 share a document date: the F-3 was declared effective 2026-08-12, the same morning as the AI-pivot press release, so the -5.99% print on 2026-08-12 that GMHS#0 would claim as its reaction is jointly attributable and cannot be assigned to either claim cleanly. (3) GMHS#1's own cited source refutes GMHS#1's sizing: the $200m ceiling is capped by the Form F-3 one-third-of-float limitation stated on the cover page to roughly $7.8m on a $23.5m non-affiliate float. Corrections to the brief and baseline, offered because they change the directional prior rather than any single verdict: (a) the brief labels 2026-06-24 as the Q3 FY26 print, but Q3 FY26 results were released 2026-06-08 (PRNewswire 302793775) and the 2026-06-24 6-K is the EGM proxy statement — so the +9.84% 'intraday' row is a governance filing, not an earnings reaction, and the usable earnings base rate is three overnight events, not four; (b) the baseline's headline analogue, '2025-09-09 annual print reacted -18.78%', looks to be off by one session and wrong-signed. The FY25 release carries a SHANGHAI Sept. 9, 2025 PRNewswire dateline and Gamehaus releases at 06:00 ET, i.e. before the open, so 2025-09-09 was the reaction day, not the day after; third-party summaries put the 2025-09-09 reaction at +32.37% (snippet-level only, via Simply Wall St / stockanalysis derived text — I could not retrieve 2025 daily bars to confirm, so I flag this as unresolved rather than assert it). If it is right, the baseline's session tag of 'amc' has captured the 2025-09-10 give-back and the closest analogue to this print reacted strongly positive on the day, which cuts against every bearish sizing above including my own.
